definitions.explanation: The seat(s) in the back of a vehicle, especially a car. Distinguished from the front passenger seat and the driver's seat.

examples.japanese: {後部|こうぶ}{座席|ざせき}に{座|すわ}る。
examples.english: To sit in the back seat.

examples.japanese: {後部|こうぶ}{座席|ざせき}のシートベルトも{必|かなら}ず{締|し}めてください。
examples.english: Please make sure to fasten your seatbelt in the back seat as well.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}は{後部|こうぶ}{座席|ざせき}に{乗|の}せて、チャイルドシートを{使用|しよう}してください。
examples.english: Please have children ride in the back seat and use a child seat.

notes:
A compound of {後部|こうぶ} (rear part) and {座席|ざせき} (seat). Primarily used for car seating but can also apply to buses and airplanes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {後部|こうぶ}{座席|ざせき}のシートベルト: back seat seatbelt
- {後部|こうぶ}{座席|ざせき}に{乗|の}る: to ride in the back seat
- {後部|こうぶ}{座席|ざせき}の{乗客|じょうきゃく}: back seat passenger

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {後|うし}ろの{席|せき}: the seat in the back — more casual and everyday expression
- {助手席|じょしゅせき}: front passenger seat — the seat next to the driver
- {運転席|うんてんせき}: driver's seat

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, wearing seatbelts in the {後部|こうぶ}{座席|ざせき} became mandatory on all roads in 2008. In taxis, VIP passengers typically sit in the {後部|こうぶ}{座席|ざせき}, with the seat directly behind the driver considered the most prestigious position.
